correctness.rationale: The statement is finite and exhaustive. The complete labelled-graph enumeration covers all 2^{n choose 2} edge masks for each 2<=n<=5, checks connectivity before and after every deleted edge, and computes exact 2^n-state consensus basins by backwards reachability from the unanimous fixed states. The independent pure-Python implementation checks every initial state by forward trajectory and separately canonicalizes all marked graphs with all 5! relabellings. Both give no qualifying pairs at order <=4, exactly 240 labelled qualifying pairs at order five and exactly two graph-and-edge types of 120 pairs each. Explicit trajectories independently witness lost and gained members for each type. Logs and complete source are included. No claim is made about all larger graphs.

originality.rationale: The precise statement is the sharp minimum order five and its two marked-isomorphism classes for *simultaneous* strict increase in the unconditional consensus basin and loss of some previously attracted states. The prior 2000 nonmonotonic democratic-correctness theorem differs in the event being measured and supplies neither the joint inequality nor this minimum. The complete-bipartite one-edge formula applies to graphs without triangles, whereas both five-vertex representatives have triangles. The Robertson and Heawood recorded graph-census claims concern other graphs and/or two-edge losses, not this minimum. Searches found no statement implying all parts of the classification. Absolute bibliographic priority is not proven.

value.rationale: The first order at which a redundant edge deletion improves aggregate eventual-unanimity frequency while destroying consensus for specific old starts is a natural sharp robustness boundary for deterministic opinion dynamics. The two complete minimum-order graph/marked-edge types and their exact lost/gained counts distinguish aggregate performance from statewise stability. The computation addresses a motivated minimum-classification question, not an arbitrary single-graph slice; no asymptotic theorem or larger-order classification is required for this exact invariant.
